title: Debugging with gdb
summary: Run a program under a debugger, see where it crashed, and stop it anywhere to look at its variables.

text: A debugger runs your program for you, and can stop it to show what's inside: which line, which calls, which values.
- Build with -g first: gdb needs the line numbers.
bt (backtrace) is the chain of calls, the newest first.
- #0 is where it died, #1 called #0, and so on down to main.
- Look at line 28 first. Then ask why its caller passed that value.
- The 0x… numbers are memory addresses: skip them for now. Read the function and the file:line.

scheme: (gdb) break month_end   stop when it starts
(gdb) continue          go to the next stop
text: - A breakpoint pauses the program at a function or a line (break loan.c:12).
- next runs one line, step goes into a call, finish comes back out.
- break month_end if month == 5 stops only when the condition is true.

scheme: gdb -tui        gdb with the source on screen
VS Code, CLion  gdb/lldb behind buttons
text: The same ideas everywhere: breakpoints, steps, variables, backtrace.
- An editor's debugger is gdb or lldb behind buttons: what you learn here carries over.
- For memory bugs, -fsanitize=address is much faster than valgrind, but needs a rebuild; valgrind works on the program as it is.
